Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-15 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 72m
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (CSM) — Cloudburst: Maya Patel (Head of ML), Tom Grady (CTO), Sofia Nguyen (Platform Eng), Ben Wallace (Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Quarterly business review focused on inference economics, reliability targets and roadmap decisions for Cloudburst's public product rollout in Q1.
- Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated pools; pilot and benchmarking plan agreed.
- Security and compliance checklist requested, pricing worksheet to be sent.

Topics (auto): usage patterns, cost optimization, SLA/uptime, dedicated sizing, security/KMS, pilot timeline, next steps

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Liam Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. This is our QBR but it is sorta a decision day right? We wanted to go through the economics and the plan — make sure we're aligned on the pilot and contract contingencies.
00:14 Maya Patel (Cloudburst): Yeah thanks Liam, we've got the execs on the line to get to a final yes. Scope is basically production inference for features A and B, and later rollouts for C. Our main constraints: latency SLOs < 120ms p95, cost target <$0.10 per 1k tokens, and strict data residency for EU customers.
00:37 Priya Rao (Redwood SE): Great summary, Maya. Quick check — the 120ms p95, is that cold-start inclusive or steady-state?
00:45 Maya Patel: Steady state, cold starts can be looser, maybe 200 to 300ms. It's the interactive UI flows that need p95 tight.
00:56 Tom Grady (CTO): And to add — we're sensitive about auditability. SOC2 is a must and we'd like to lock in audit log retention for 12 months. Ben, confirm budget?
01:08 Ben Wallace (Finance): We're modeling a three-tier commit: small pilot, then mid reserved, then full reserved for 12 months. Budget line is draft but we need an assumption on unit cost to sign.
01:21 Liam Chen: Understood. High level: Redwood Hosted gives fastest time-to-value; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better unit economics for sustained load. For your numbers — we ran a projection based on the usage you shared in Oct. If you hit 400M gen tokens/mo, Dedicated with an optimized quantized model hits around $0.07 per 1k tokens. Hosted baseline is closer to $0.12 unless we use burst credits.
01:48 Sofia Nguyen (Platform Eng): Wait — can you break down the assumptions? Sequence length, batching, and cache hit rates change cost a lot. What did you assume for p50/p95 token lengths?
01:58 Priya Rao: Good call. For the model in our catalog we used a 512-seq average with 12-token responses, batching factor ~8, and a cache hit of 25% on prompts. If you can increase prefix reuse to 40% we push unit cost lower by ~12%. But that depends on your workload shape.
02:18 Maya Patel: Our current average is 400 tokens request, 18 tokens response, but that includes long-context analytics. For the UI interactive bits it's smaller; we can probably tile those into a separate route.
02:32 Liam Chen: That's a common pattern — split routes by intent. It also lets you route interactive flows to lower-latency Dedicated pools and analytics to cost-optimized hosted endpoints or separate batch windows.
02:45 Tom Grady: Security wise — if we go Dedicated in our VPC, what does the control plane look like? How much of the telemetry leaves our tenancy?
02:55 Priya Rao: With Redwood Private/Dedicated we can run the inference plane in your VPC. The control plane (optional) is a small management endpoint — we can offer a private-only control plane in the Private product. Telemetry for billing and high-level metrics can be forwarded to Redwood, but we also support customer-side metrics via Prometheus exporters and full audit logs stored into your S3.
03:18 Sofia Nguyen: KMS integration? We need HSM-backed keys and rotation policy.
03:24 Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood supports external KMS and HSM via standard integrations; we can align rotation with your policies. We'll add the KMS diagram in the security bundle.
03:33 Ben Wallace: Okay for procurement — if the pilot shows the numbers, what's the cadence to move to 12mo reserved? Any early-exit penalties?
03:41 Liam Chen: We can propose a contract with a 60-day pilot period and a commitment window starting after pilot. Standard reserved pricing includes early termination clauses but we can structure a ramp with credits applied towards the commitment if you convert. We'll put specifics in the worksheet.
03:55 Maya Patel: Let's talk reliability — redundant regions, failover time. We need cross-region failover for EU to US in case of outages, but data residency needs mean EU customers must not leave region for normal traffic. Failover has to be opt-in per customer.
04:12 Priya Rao: Smart routing can handle region + tier fallback. You can pin EU accounts to EU region with an auto-fallback to a compliant region if you flip the flag; we can also do read-only fallbacks for non-sensitive paths.
04:26 Tom Grady: Performance testing — can Redwood run a litmus test that simulates our spike patterns? Our peak is 3x baseline for 6 hours daily during promotions.
04:36 Priya Rao: Yep. That's exactly what the two-week pilot benchmark will cover: steady-state, 3x spike, long-tail sequences, and cache effectiveness. We'll instrument latency, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization.
04:51 Daniel Ortiz (CSM): Quick note — during the last quarter we tracked two incidents where p99 latency spiked due to batch underruns; Priya's team did an autotune but we'd like recommendations to avoid that.
05:02 Priya Rao: Batch underruns happen when traffic is too bursty — solutions: adaptive batching thresholds, jitter smoothing, or short-lived warm pools. For Dedicated we can reserve additional warm capacity for interactive routes.
05:18 Sofia Nguyen: Warm pools sound expensive. Can you quantify?
05:23 Priya Rao: Depends on sizing; warm pools for a route that represents 20% of traffic might add 8–12% to monthly cost but reduce p95 by ~30–40ms. We'll model that in the pricing worksheet.
05:37 Ben Wallace: That's acceptable if it's predictable.
05:41 Maya Patel: Anything about model updates? We need rollout safety for new model versions — can we do canaries and automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops?
05:50 Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, traffic splitting, and automatic fallback policy based on latency/error/quality regressions. You can bind evals to prompt sets so a degredation triggers an automatic rollback.
06:06 Tom Grady: How are quality regressions detected? We need deterministic metrics — fuzzy BLEU isn't enough.
06:12 Priya Rao: Our recommended approach uses task-specific evals and signal sets — your prompt library + golden labels for the top flows. We'll run regen tests and compare metrics; threshold breaches can be configured.
06:24 Maya Patel: Good. Now, the pilot — timeline? We proposed start 11/27, two weeks with the test harness. Who owns infra provisioning on our side?
06:33 Sofia Nguyen: We'll own VPC setup and peering. We expect Redwood engineers to help with initial network verification and KMS binding.
06:41 Priya Rao: That works. Priya will pair with Sofia on day 1, we'll need the traffic samples and a staging token. Also, please provide your traffic shape JSON and any route definitions.
06:53 Sofia Nguyen: I'll share the traffic histogram and current p95 numbers by 11/20.
07:00 Ben Wallace: Last thing — procurement needs an indicative T&Cs doc and a SOW for the pilot. Can't sign without it.
07:07 Liam Chen: We'll share a redline-friendly SOW and the T&Cs bundle after this call.
07:12 Maya Patel: Ok let's recap — pilot plan, pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, exec sync next week. Anything else?
07:18 Liam Chen: That's it from our side. Thanks everyone.
